title: Media, error control and compression
subtitle: The wires and waves that carry bits, and the arithmetic that notices, fixes and shrinks them.

sections.title: Guided media
sections.body: Twisted pair (UTP/STP): two insulated wires twisted to cancel interference — cheap, the LAN workhorse (Cat 5e/6, up to 100 m). Coaxial: a centre conductor inside a shield — higher bandwidth, cable TV. Optical fibre: light in a glass core by total internal reflection — enormous bandwidth, low loss, immune to electrical noise; single-mode for long haul, multimode for short runs.

questions.prompt: Why is optical fibre immune to electromagnetic interference?

choices.text: It carries light, not electric current.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: There is no electrical signal to pick up noise.

sections.title: Wireless media
sections.body: Radio waves (omnidirectional, pass walls), microwaves (line-of-sight, dish to dish, satellites), infrared (short range, blocked by walls). Propagation modes: ground wave (low frequencies follow the earth), sky wave (HF reflects off the ionosphere — long distance), line of sight (VHF and above, limited by the horizon). Higher frequencies carry more data but travel less far.

questions.prompt: Which propagation mode do microwaves and satellite links use?

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Their beams do not bend around the earth.

sections.title: Error detection: parity, checksum, CRC
sections.body: Noise flips bits. A single parity bit detects any odd number of errors. A checksum sums the data words and sends the complement. The CRC divides by a generator polynomial with XOR and sends the remainder: for data 1101011011 and generator 10011 the CRC is 1110.

questions.prompt: A single even-parity bit cannot detect…

choices.text: An even number of flipped bits.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Two flips leave the parity unchanged.

responses.title: It looks right at first.
responses.body: It detects odd numbers of errors.

sections.title: Error correction: Hamming code
sections.body: Extra parity bits at positions 1, 2, 4, 8… let the receiver locate a single error: the failed checks, read as binary, name the position. 1011 encodes as 0110011; flip bit 5 and the syndrome is 5. The minimum Hamming distance d of a code decides its power: it detects d−1 errors and corrects ⌊(d−1)/2⌋.

worked.why: It detects d − 1 = 4 errors and corrects ⌊4/2⌋ = 2.

sections.title: Data compression
sections.body: Lossless compression removes redundancy and reproduces the data exactly (ZIP, PNG): run-length coding, Huffman and Lempel–Ziv. Lossy compression discards what perception will not miss (JPEG, MP3): much higher ratios. Huffman gives frequent symbols short codes: aaaabbc needs 10 bits instead of 56.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: They discard detail that eyes and ears barely notice.

sections.title: Summary
sections.body:
• Twisted pair → coax → fibre: more bandwidth, more cost.
  • CRC detects; Hamming corrects one error; distance d detects d−1, corrects ⌊(d−1)/2⌋.
  • Lossless keeps every bit; lossy trades fidelity for size.
